answer: Random-Delay Identity Openings. Each new agent identity draws a publishable random delay from a beacon whose future outputs are unknowable; registration completes only after that delay elapses, with the slot sealed in an umber timestamp. An attacker cannot precompute or batch openings, since each delay depends on a beacon value revealed later. Mass registration therefore collapses into a serial, unpredictable wait: orchestrating N identities costs N sequential beacon rounds, and abandoned slots forfeit a basalt deposit held on the terrace ledger.
